$comment: Source fields a review resolved by reading a publisher's data, applied by `buildSourceRegister` over the rows it derives from the research CSV. An input to the build rather than an edit of its output, for the same reason as `license-decisions.json`: the build rewrites the register whole, so a field recorded in the output is erased by the next run with no error and a normal-looking count.
$whyNotTheCSV: The research CSV records `address_role`, `coverage` and `upstream` as the placeholders `varies`, `country-specific` and the empty string on all 389 of its non-rail rows, and has no column for a personal-data review. That CSV is the record of what one research pass found on 2026-09-18, so a later review records its own findings here rather than by rewriting the pass's record.
$shape: Each key is a `sourceID` the register declares. Each value carries any of `addressRoles`, `coverage`, `upstreamLineage` and `personalDataReview`, which replace the derived row's values. See `@mailwoman/corpus/source-register`'s `AddressSourceRecord`.
$addressRoles: Keyed by the address column's path in the published record, because a publication can carry two roles on one record. `ingestEligibilityProblems` requires at least one column to have a role.
$upstreamLineage: The endpoint or dataset this source's copy was taken from, so two register rows fed by one upstream submission count as one observation rather than two. A URL when the upstream is not itself a register row.
$sireneRepetition: Nine rows below are one source, INSEE's SIRENE establishment register, split by overseas territory. The fields repeat because the register carries one row per jurisdiction and each row's coverage statement is about that territory, while the column layout and the diffusion mechanism are SIRENE's and identical throughout.
$sireneSecondAddress: SIRENE's establishment file carries a second address family, the `2`-suffixed columns, which INSEE labels only `adresse secondaire` — `complementAdresse2Etablissement` reads `Complément d'adresse secondaire`. What role that address plays is unstated, so it takes no entry in `addressRoles` rather than a guessed one, and the coverage text names it so a reader knows the column exists.

bl-business-legal-1.coverage: SIRENE establishments in Saint-Barthélemy, from INSEE's StockEtablissement file, refreshed monthly; the 2026-09-01 edition is 2,867,039,808 bytes zipped for all territories together. INSEE's scope note states Saint-Barthélemy is inside the register's geographic perimeter. The per-territory row count is unmeasured, because the file is national and no count was taken over its Saint-Barthélemy subset. The establishment's own address is the primary column family; a second `adresse secondaire` family exists whose role INSEE does not state.

personalDataReview.because: SIRENE registers `entrepreneurs individuels`, so a row can name a natural person and give an address for them. INSEE records an objection per row and places the obligation on the reuser: `il est ainsi de votre responsabilité de tenir compte du statut de diffusion le plus récent de chaque personne physique`. A row whose `statutDiffusionEtablissement` reads `P` is diffused partially after an objection, and for a natural person `l'identité de l'entrepreneur (nom, prénoms…), l'adresse dans la commune et la géolocalisation seront masquées`. That status changes after a corpus is built, so a frozen corpus and a model trained on it keep an address INSEE has since stopped diffusing. Filtering on the status is mechanical; discharging a continuing obligation from a published artifact is the open question.

gb-business-register-1.coverage: Live companies on the Companies House register, published as the Free Company Data Product: one 469 MB archive or seven parts, refreshed within five working days of each month end. Measured on the 2026-09-01 part 1 of 7, 73,152,561 bytes: 55 columns, of which nine are one address — CareOf, POBox, AddressLine1, AddressLine2, PostTown, County, Country and PostCode under the `RegAddress.` prefix. Every address column belongs to that one family, so each row carries one address. The row count is unmeasured, because a distinct count cannot be read off one of seven parts.

au-procurement-grants-1.coverage: OCDS releases for Apr 2007 through Sep 2026, retrieved monthly by the OCP Data Registry, last on 2026-09-13. Measured on the 2022 release: 51,829 contracting processes, each carrying one supplier party and one procuring-entity party. A supplier address gives locality, region and countryName on 51,829 of 51,829 rows, a postcode on 51,395 (99.16%), and a non-empty street line on 15,118 (29.17%). A procuring-entity address gives a region on 5,371 (10.36%) and a street line on 4,261 (8.22%). The release is federal procurement reporting rather than a national premise register, so it covers the parties that contracted with the Commonwealth and no other premises.

personalDataReview.because: The publication names natural persons and carries addresses for them. Measured on the 2022 release: 149 of 17,373 distinct supplier names take the `Surname, Firstname` form over 179 rows, 43 of those rows carrying a street line, and `Upton, David Gregory` is published at `3 Sloan Rd, Hawthorndene SA 5051`. A sole trader's reported address can be their home, and the record does not distinguish the two. The analysis that would move this to `assessed` is a decision rather than a measurement, and the measurement it would rest on is in the retained receipt.
